source.name: MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise
source.note: The plain-language texts (short, analogy and the Ukrainian names) are CyberPlain’s adaptation (CC BY 4.0). IDs, English names and order come from MITRE ATT&CK.

intro.title: A map of how an attacker operates.
intro.lead: MITRE ATT&CK is an open knowledge base of real cyberattacks. It is maintained by the nonprofit MITRE, and filled in by incident-response specialists from all over the world.
intro.body: The knowledge base describes not viruses or products but behavior: what an attacker does, step by step. That’s why it’s used by those who attack in training exercises, by those who defend, and by the makers of security tools.

terms.title: The table of the whole knowledge base.
terms.text: The columns are the stages of an attack; each column lists the ways that stage is carried out.

terms.title: Why.
terms.text: The attacker’s goal at a given stage: get inside, gain a foothold, steal data.

terms.title: How.
terms.text: A specific way to reach that goal. A single tactic usually has dozens.

terms.title: How exactly.
terms.text: An even more specific variant of a technique.

intro.sectionLead: Read it in a zigzag — the way a typical attack unfolds. Click a stage to see its techniques.
intro.caveat: This is a map, not a route. A real attack may skip stages, repeat them or go in a different order.
